Hi Alex —

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and a few asks so we can put together a targeted pricing proposal: 

Summary of use case (as I understood it):
- Primary: conversational assistant (multi-turn chat) for internal support + customer-facing 
- Secondary: short-form embeddings for search/ranking (~10% of tokens)
- Latency SLO: <500ms for chat median, some async batching for embeddings

What we discussed we need from you to finalize pricing:
1) Expected steady-state token volume (tokens/day or tokens/month). You mentioned large volume on peak days — any rough peak vs average ratio?
2) Target budget range per month (high level is fine).
3) Procurement timeline & decision owner(s).
4) Any requirement for Dedicated/Private deployment (VPC, data residency).

On pricing benchmarking: our team will include a quick comparator of $/1M tokens vs major hosts (OpenAI/Anthropic/other open-model hosts) and propose a target tier that meets your budget. If you have a target $/1M we should aim for, please share it — that helps us shape committed vs pilot pricing.

I'll attach our simple pricing worksheet for reference (see redwood-pricing-sheet.xlsx).

Next steps: if you can reply with the items above, we'll turn around a draft proposal + pilot offer by EOD Wed.

Thanks,

Thanks Vanessa — quick answers below. Appreciate the fast follow-up.

1) Volumes: baseline ~50M tokens/day (~1.5B tokens/month). Peak events (release days) could be ~2x baseline for short windows.
2) Budget: we're targeting roughly $18k-$25k/month initially; stretch budget could go to $40k/mo if unit economics are there.
3) Timeline: procurement decision expected by end of May; pilot in May if we can get legal/infosec review done. Decision owner is me (Alex) with procurement lead Sarah Mills.
4) Deployment: prefer hosted for pilot, but will evaluate Dedicated for production if prices and SLAs align.

Target $/1M tokens: our internal goal is ~$12/1M tokens effective. If Redwood can present a committed pricing path that gets near that number for steady-state volumes, we can accelerate.

Let me know if you need any more detail.

Thanks Vanessa — notes and proposed approach below. Putting the quick comparator up front so you have numbers for the customer call: 

Typical $/1M benchmarks (ballpark, hosted inference public pricing or market averages):
- OpenAI (gpt-4 style / high capability): ~$20-$40 / 1M tokens (depends on model & context length) — higher for latest models.
- Anthropic (Claude-like): ~$18-$30 / 1M tokens depending on model and throughput.
- Other open-model hosts / managed open model providers: ranges vary widely — roughly $6-$15 / 1M tokens for optimized open models on shared hosted tiers, but those numbers often exclude infra egress/ops in the SOW or assume lower SLOs.
- Self-hosted / infra-only: infra costs can push effective $/1M to $4-$12 depending on utilization, but you take on ops, reliability, and autoscaling risk.

Redwood positioning and recommended offer:
- Hosted (open-model optimized): baseline public tier we can show at $14/1M for their volume bands; with a 12-month commit at 1B tokens/mo, we can get to an effective $9/1M.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): predictable throughput + better unit economics — we can price down to $7-$8 / 1M for true reserved commitments (1B+/mo) with SLA.
- Pilot recommendation to hit Alex's target ($12/1M): offer a 3-month pilot at $10/1M up to 500M tokens/month (hosted), and include a credit structure or ramp: commit to 1B/mo for a 12-month contract with step-down to $8.5/1M after month 3. That yields an effective blended $9-$10/1M for the first year depending on ramp.

Caveats / talking points to share with ACME:
- Caching & batching: enabling prefix/KV caching for assistant calls and workload-aware batching will materially reduce effective tokens billed; we should propose an eval to measure prefix hit rates.
- Model selection: latency and cost tradeoffs — using a smaller optimized open model for assistant could reduce $/1M while meeting SLOs for many flows. We should include a short A/B on model variants.
- Sizing assumptions: the $7-$9/1M Dedicated numbers assume sustained, committed usage and predictable throughput. Bursty traffic or very high tail latency SLOs can increase cost.

Attachments: I drafted a short one-pager proposal (acme-proposal-v1.pdf) that outlines the pilot + committed pricing and the value levers (caching, batching, Dedicated option).

Suggested next steps for Vanessa to send to Alex: 
1) Send pilot proposal (3 months at $10/1M up to 500M tokens/month) and invite for a technical eval with our SREs to instrument caching/batching.
2) Offer a path to convert to a 12-month commit at 1B/mo with step-down pricing to $8.5/1M; include an SLA addendum.
3) Start legal/infosec packet for hosted pilot; escalate to Dedicated if they insist on VPC.

If you want, I can also prepare a line-item comparison vs OpenAI/Anthropic to include in the customer email.

Marissa Cole
